title: Chasing the Scream: The First and Last Days of the War on Drugs
author: Johann Hari
target_audience: Individuals interested in drug policy and social issues
Students and scholars of criminology, sociology, or public health
Readers seeking narrative nonfiction with in-depth reporting
core_themes: History and origins of the global war on drugs
Addiction, stigma, and public perception of drug users
Compassion, human rights, and social justice
primary_purpose: To investigate the history, impact, and human cost of the War on Drugs, challenging mainstream assumptions and exploring the roots of drug prohibition while highlighting stories of individuals affected by related policies.

structure_format.narrative_style: Engaging, story-driven investigative journalism, weaving together historical research, personal stories, and interviews
structure_format.organization: Divided into three main sections and numerous chapters, each focusing on a particular theme or individual story
features: Use of anecdotal evidence alongside academic research

key_concepts_lessons: The War on Drugs was shaped significantly by individuals with personal motivations and prejudices.
Criminalization of drugs has led to widespread social and humanitarian harm, including mass incarceration and marginalization.
Addiction is deeply connected to issues of trauma, social isolation, and lack of connection, rather than simply the properties of drugs themselves.
Policy approaches based on compassion, decriminalization, and treatment (such as Portugal’s drug policy) can lead to positive public health outcomes.
Social narratives and myths about drugs and addiction often overshadow scientific evidence.
notable_features: Blends personal narrative with historical research
Profiles a range of characters—from law enforcement agents to addicts and activists
Covers international contexts (US, UK, Mexico, Canada, Portugal, etc.)
Influence on later works, including the documentary series adaptation
Reframes addiction through a lens of empathy and social connection
cultural_historical_context: Published during growing global debate about drug policy reform, the book critically examines a century of prohibition policies beginning in the U.S. and their worldwide impact. It draws on contemporary shifts toward decriminalization in places like Portugal and changing attitudes about addiction science.
reception_impact: International bestseller and widely acclaimed for narrative style and depth of research
Praised for humanizing drug users and shedding light on overlooked aspects of drug policy
Instrumental in shaping public discourse around drug decriminalization and harm reduction
Critics note occasional simplification of complex issues and debates over sources, but generally regarded as a seminal work in drug policy literature
comparable_titles: The New Jim Crow by Michelle Alexander
Drug War Heresies by Robert MacCoun and Peter Reuter
High Price by Dr. Carl Hart
Smoke Signals by Martin A. Lee
